ready_drafts.title: Fine cloth, once it is lost
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: While it was there, a rag; once lost, a fine cloth.
ready_drafts.explanation: The object changes in the speaker’s estimation after it disappears. What was dismissed as a torn rag suddenly becomes fine cloth worth lamenting. The joke catches the difference between the care something received and the value claimed for it afterwards. In an everyday application, it can tease exaggerated regret over an object or opportunity that was taken for granted. That application is our close reading of the contrast; the dictionary supplies the saying and the cloth vocabulary, not an account of its first use.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ପାଖରେ ଥିବାବେଳେ ଯାହାକୁ ଚିରାକନା କହି ତୁଚ୍ଛ କରାଯାଉଥିଲା, ହଜିଗଲା ପରେ ସେଇଟି ମାଠ ହୋଇଯାଉଛି। ବଦଳିଛି ଜିନିଷଟି ନୁହେଁ, ତାହାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ବିଷୟରେ କହୁଥିବା ମଣିଷର କଥା। ଥିବାବେଳେ ଆଦର ନ କରି ହରାଇବା ପରେ ବହୁତ ଆଦର ଦେଖାଇବାକୁ ଏହି ଓଲଟା ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଧରିହୁଏ। ଏଠାରେ ସେହି ହାଲୁକା କଟାକ୍ଷକୁ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ଅବହେଳା ଓ ଅନୁତାପର ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
ready_drafts.english_summary: Something dismissed while available becomes precious once it is lost.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ପାଖରେ ଥିବାବେଳେ ଅବହେଳିତ ଜିନିଷ ହଜିଗଲେ ହଠାତ୍ ମୂଲ୍ୟବାନ ଲାଗେ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: A brother has called an old scarf useless for months. When he misplaces it, he calls it his finest scarf. His sister laughs and quotes the saying, reminding him how he spoke about it yesterday.

ready_drafts.title: Calling a free thing costly
ready_drafts.explanation: The dictionary gives a specific occasion for this short taunt: someone receives something without paying and still calls it expensive. The absurd price complaint does the work. A speaker can use it to prick dissatisfaction that forgets what was actually paid. It is not the different saying that a free offer always carries a hidden cost; neither does it settle whether the thing is useful or whether the recipient may refuse it. Its bite lies in this particular mismatch between receiving gratis and complaining about the price.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: କିଛି ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନ ଦେଇ ଜିନିଷଟି ମିଳିଛି, ତଥାପି ତାହା ମହର୍ଗ ବୋଲି ଅଭିଯୋଗ ହେଉଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଅସଙ୍ଗତି ପାଇଁ କଥାଟି କୁହାଯାଏ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଇଛି। ଦୁଇ ପଦରେ ମିଳିଥିବା ସୁବିଧା ଓ ଅଭିଯୋଗର ହିସାବକୁ ସାମ୍ନାସାମ୍ନି ରଖିଦିଏ। ଜିନିଷଟି ଭଲ କି ଖରାପ, ସେ ବିଚାର ଅଲଗା; ଏଠାରେ କଟାକ୍ଷଟି ହେଉଛି ଟଙ୍କା ନ ଦେଇ ଦାମ ବିଷୟରେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିବା ଉପରେ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: The taunt targets someone who pays nothing but complains that the price is high.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନ ଦେଇ ପାଇଥିବା ଜିନିଷର ଦାମକୁ ନେଇ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିବାରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: A club gives away its spare notebooks. Someone accepts one, then jokingly complains that it was too expensive. The organiser replies, “ମାଗଣୁ ମହର୍ଗ,” and both laugh at the impossible bill.

ready_drafts.title: No one calls me into the shade
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: I sit in the fierce sun; they do not say, “Come into the shade.”
ready_drafts.explanation: This voice complains of a small kindness withheld. The speaker is exposed to fierce heat, while the wished-for response is only an invitation into shade. The line makes neglect tangible without telling us who the others are or why they remain silent. Read conversationally, it can express the hurt of being overlooked when someone could easily acknowledge a difficulty. That broader use follows the image; it is not a documented original occasion or a claim that every unspoken offer is deliberate cruelty.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଚଣ୍ଡ ଖରାରେ ବସିଥିବା ମଣିଷଟି ଅନେକ କିଛି ମାଗୁନାହିଁ; ଛାଇକୁ ଆସ ବୋଲି ପଦେ ଡାକକୁ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରୁଛି। ସେ ଡାକ ନ ମିଳିବାରେ ଅଭିମାନ ରହିଛି। ଦେଖିପାରୁଥିବା କଷ୍ଟ ପ୍ରତି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଧ୍ୟାନ ନ ଦେବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରେ। କିଏ ଡାକିଲେ ନାହିଁ ବା ସେମାନଙ୍କ ସହ କି ସମ୍ପର୍କ, ପଦଟି ନିଜେ ତାହା କହେନାହିଁ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: The speaker feels overlooked when even a simple invitation to shelter is missing.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: କଷ୍ଟ ଦେଖି ମଧ୍ୟ ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଆଶ୍ରୟକୁ ଡାକ ନ ମିଳିବାର ଅଭିମାନ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: After helping arrange an outdoor meeting, a volunteer remains in the sun while the others sit under the canopy. Later the volunteer quotes the line to a friend, describing the hurt of not being invited to join them.

ready_drafts.title: When an unasked-for gift loses value
ready_drafts.explanation: The dictionary explains “no colour” here as a lack of value: an unsolicited thing is not valued. The line points to reception rather than a defect in the object. Something offered without being requested may be overlooked precisely because no effort was made to seek it. Our reading treats that as an observation about undervaluing what arrives easily, not proof that unsolicited help or gifts are worthless. It can sound rueful from the giver or self-mocking from someone who recognises their own neglect.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ଯାଚିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ମିଳିଥିବା ଜିନିଷର “ରଙ୍ଗ ନାହିଁ”—ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ଏହାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନ ହେବାର କଥା ଅଛି। ଜିନିଷଟିର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଗୁଣ ଠାରୁ ଏଠାରେ ତାହାକୁ କେମିତି ଗ୍ରହଣ କରାଯାଉଛି, ସେଇଟି ଆଗକୁ ଆସେ। ଖୋଜିବାକୁ ବା ମାଗିବାକୁ ନ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ମିଳିଥିବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟକୁ ହାଲୁକା ଭାବେ ନେବାରେ ଏହି କଥା ଲାଗିପାରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହା ସେହି ଅବହେଳାକୁ ଧରେ, ନ ମାଗି ମିଳିଥିବା ସବୁ ଜିନିଷ ମୂଲ୍ୟହୀନ ବୋଲି ରାୟ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: An unsolicited offering may receive less regard than something actively sought.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ନ ମାଗି ମିଳିଥିବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ବା ଜିନିଷର ଆଦର କମିଯାଇପାରେ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: A colleague sends useful notes before anyone asks. They remain unread until the team pays for similar guidance elsewhere. The colleague quotes the saying with a rueful smile about the notes that arrived too easily.

ready_drafts.title: Searching the wrong pond
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: Like losing something in a small tank and searching for it in a pond.
ready_drafts.explanation: The search has moved away from the place of the loss. A larger or more noticeable place will not become the right one simply because it attracts attention. As an analogy, the image can question effort directed at the wrong location or cause. It asks the listener to connect the search with what actually happened before continuing. The source defines the small tank and labels the comparison; this explanation extends the spatial mismatch into an everyday use, without claiming a particular lost object or origin story.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ଜିନିଷଟି ହଜିଛି ଗାଡ଼ିଆରେ, ଖୋଜା ଚାଲିଛି ପୋଖରୀରେ। ଖୋଜିବାର ପରିଶ୍ରମ ଥିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ସ୍ଥାନର ମେଳ ନାହିଁ। କେଉଁଠି ଭୁଲ ହେଲା ନ ଦେଖି ଅନ୍ୟଠାରେ ଉତ୍ତର ଖୋଜିବାକୁ ଆମେ ଏହି ତୁଳନାରେ ବୁଝିପାରୁ। ଆଉ ଅଧିକ ଖୋଜିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଖୋଜାର ଦିଗଟି ଠିକ୍ କି ନାହିଁ, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠେ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: Effort misses its mark when the search is detached from where the loss occurred.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ଯେଉଁଠି ହଜିଛି ତାହା ଛାଡ଼ି ଅନ୍ୟଠାରେ ଖୋଜିଲେ ପରିଶ୍ରମ ଠିକ୍ ଦିଗରେ ଯାଏନାହିଁ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: A team keeps checking the delivery van for a missing parcel, although its own register says the parcel never left the store. One member quotes the analogy and asks them to begin with the store records.

ready_drafts.title: Giving, and closing the door
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: Give to the giver; close the door to the non-giver.
ready_drafts.explanation: The repeated sound of “ଦିଆ” changes its force at the door: giving becomes shutting someone out. Read as a compact rule of reciprocity, the line divides people according to whether they give. It can expose the calculating side of an exchange in which welcome depends on a return. Our reading leaves room for a speaker to endorse that bargain or mock it; the short dictionary quotation supplies no performance setting. It should not be turned into a rule that someone unable to contribute deserves exclusion.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଥମେ “ଦିଆ”ରେ ଦେବାର କଥା, ଶେଷରେ “ଦୁଆର ଦିଆ”ରେ ବାଟ ବନ୍ଦ କରିବାର କଥା ଆସୁଛି। ଯିଏ ଦିଏ ତାକୁ ଦିଅ, ଯିଏ ଦିଏନାହିଁ ତାହା ପାଇଁ ଦୁଆର ବନ୍ଦ—ଏହି ହିସାବଟି କଥାରେ ଧରାପଡ଼େ। ଆଦର ଓ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଯେତେବେଳେ କେବଳ ପ୍ରତିଦାନ ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କରେ, ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ତାହାର ସଂକୀର୍ଣ୍ଣତା ମଧ୍ୟ ଦିଶେ। ଏହାକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ କରି କୁହାଗଲା କି କଟାକ୍ଷରେ, ଅଭିଧାନର ଛୋଟ ଉଦାହରଣ ସେ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: The sound-play turns reciprocity into a door that opens or closes according to what someone gives.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ଦେବାର ହିସାବରେ ଦୁଆର ଖୋଲିବା ବା ବନ୍ଦ ହେବାର ଶବ୍ଦଖେଳ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: A committee suggests helping only members who donated last year. Another member quotes the saying critically, then asks what happens to neighbours who had nothing to give.

ready_drafts.title: Even the wise differ
ready_drafts.explanation: The repetition makes disagreement unsurprising: several thinkers need not arrive at one view. The line can loosen a conversation that has stalled because each side expects complete agreement. It does not tell us that all opinions are equally well supported, or that a decision can be avoided forever. Rather, in our reading, it creates a little room to hear why people differ before choosing what to do. The dictionary supplies “different opinions” and this example; it identifies no particular sages or dispute.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ମୁନି ଅନେକ ହେଲେ ମତ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅନେକ ହୋଇପାରେ। “ନାନା”ର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତିରେ ମତଭେଦକୁ ଆଶ୍ଚର୍ଯ୍ୟର କଥା ନ କରି ସହଜ ଭାବେ କୁହାଯାଏ। ସମସ୍ତେ ଏକ କଥା କହିବା ଦରକାର ବୋଲି ଜିଦ୍ ଧରିଥିବା ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ଏହା ଟିକିଏ ଅବକାଶ ଆଣିପାରେ। ତଥାପି କେଉଁ ମତ ପଛରେ କି ଯୁକ୍ତି ଅଛି, ସେହି ବିଚାର କରିବାର କାମ ରହିଯାଏ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: Disagreement can remain even among thoughtful people.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ବିଚାରଶୀଳ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ମଧ୍ୟ ମତଭେଦ ରହିପାରେ।

ready_drafts.title: The sound and sweat of work
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: The dheṅki falls thump-thump; service to the sahib is very hard; sweat streams.
ready_drafts.explanation: The heavy beat of the pounding implement is answered by the sound of streaming sweat. Between them comes the complaint that service to the sahib is hard. Sound makes the labour felt before any abstract judgment is offered. The line can be read as a rhythmic complaint about demanding work, but the quotation does not identify an employer, worker or event. A present-day speaker may borrow its exaggerated beat to describe a tiring task; that is a new use, not evidence of a particular historical labour arrangement.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ଢିଙ୍କିର “ଧମଧମ” ଶବ୍ଦ ପରେ ଝାଳର “ଗମଗମ” ଆସୁଛି। ମଝିରେ ସାହାବଙ୍କ ଚାକିରି କେତେ କଠିନ, ସେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ ରହିଛି। ଶବ୍ଦର ତାଳରେ କାମର ଭାର ଓ ଶରୀରର କ୍ଳାନ୍ତି ଏକାଠି ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଆଜି କେହି ନିଜର କଠିନ କାମକୁ ନେଇ ଏହା କହିଲେ ପୁରୁଣା ଚିତ୍ରଟି ନୂଆ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗକୁ ଆସେ; କିନ୍ତୁ ମୂଳ ପଦର କର୍ମୀ ବା ସାହାବଙ୍କ ପରିଚୟ ଆମ ପାଖରେ ନାହିଁ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: Thumping sound and streaming sweat turn a complaint about hard service into a rhythmic line.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ଢିଙ୍କିର ଶବ୍ଦ ଓ ଝାଳର ଚିତ୍ରରେ କଠିନ ଚାକିରିର ଅଭିଯୋଗ ତାଳ ପାଏ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: After repeatedly moving heavy boxes for a demanding organiser, a volunteer recites the line to a friend, tapping out “ଧମଧମ.” The friend hears both the joke and the complaint about the workload.

ready_drafts.title: What a guarantee can ask of you
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: One has climbed the tree to die; one has stood surety to pay.
ready_drafts.explanation: The line states possible consequences with deliberately bleak certainty. Climbing brings the danger of a fall; standing surety can leave the guarantor having to pay. The dictionary defines the latter as undertaking responsibility for another person’s action. Our reading hears a warning against treating such an undertaking as empty words. It does not say that every climb is fatal or establish the legal effect of any present-day guarantee. The two compressed clauses make responsibility difficult to wave away.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ଗଛରେ ଚଢ଼ିବା ସହ ମୃତ୍ୟୁ, ଜାମିନ ହେବା ସହ ଟଙ୍କା ଦେବାକୁ ପଦଟି ସିଧା ଯୋଡ଼ିଦିଏ। ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପରିଣାମକୁ ଏତେ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ଭାବେ କହିବାରେ ସତର୍କ କରିବାର ଜୋର ଅଛି। ଅନ୍ୟର କାମର ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନେଲେ ସେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନିଜ ପାଖକୁ ଫେରିଆସିପାରେ—ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହାହିଁ ମୁଖ୍ୟ କଥା। କେବଳ ପଦେ ହଁ କହିଦେବା ଓ ତାହାର ଭାର ବୋହିବା ଏକ କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: A promise to answer for another person can bring a real burden back to the guarantor.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନେବାର କଥା ନିଜ ଉପରେ ପ୍ରକୃତ ଭାର ଆଣିପାରେ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: A friend agrees to cover a group’s equipment bill if the others cannot pay, calling it a mere formality. Another quotes the saying and asks whether the friend has considered actually meeting that bill.
ready_drafts.cultural_context: The stark death clause is rhetorical, not a prediction or safety instruction. Surety definition is historical lexical evidence; application is not current legal or financial advice. No actual contract is assessed.

ready_drafts.title: There is no shame in earning a living
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: Feed yourself; there is no fault.
ready_drafts.explanation: The rhyme answers an accusation before it grows: maintaining oneself is not in itself a fault. The dictionary explains “feeding the belly” as supporting one’s life. In an ordinary conversation, the line can defend necessary work against snobbery about its status. That reading concerns the dignity of earning a living, not permission to harm others for gain. The short source supplies no trade, worker or occasion, so a particular occupation belongs to an illustrative example rather than to the saying’s documented history.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ପେଟ ପୋଷିବାର ଅର୍ଥ ଅଭିଧାନରେ ନିଜର ଜୀବିକା ଚଳାଇବା। “ପୋଷ” ଓ “ଦୋଷ”ର ମେଳରେ ଜୀବିକାର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ପାଇଁ ଛୋଟ ଏକ ସମର୍ଥନ ମିଳେ। କାମଟିକୁ ହୀନ ଭାବି କେହି ହସିଲେ, ନିଜ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ନିଜେ ଚଳାଇବାରେ ଲାଜ କାହିଁକି ବୋଲି ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଆମର ଏହି ପଢ଼ା ଜୀବିକାର ସମ୍ମାନକୁ ନେଇ; ଲାଭ ପାଇଁ ଅନ୍ୟର କ୍ଷତି କରିବାକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ କରେନାହିଁ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: Earning one’s living is not itself something to be ashamed of.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ନିଜ ଜୀବିକା ଚଳାଇବାରେ ଲଜ୍ଜା ବା ଦୋଷ ନାହିଁ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: A student is embarrassed that acquaintances have seen her selling repaired furniture to support her studies. Her aunt quotes the saying, affirming the work rather than measuring its social prestige.
ready_drafts.cultural_context: Livelihood is the explicit lexical sense. Dignity against occupational snobbery is editorial application, not a named movement, historical event or licence for wrongdoing.

ready_drafts.title: The everyday edge tells a story
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: A village’s reputation is known from the washer’s bathing or washing place.
ready_drafts.explanation: The dictionary glosses the village’s “fragrance” as its greatness or reputation. The saying locates a clue to that reputation in an ordinary washing place rather than in a grand announcement. Our reading takes this as a contrast between what is claimed and what everyday surroundings reveal. It can encourage looking at a shared, practical corner before accepting a polished description. It does not supply a sanitary test or establish that the whole character of a community can be judged from one place.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଗାଁର “ପରିମଳ” ମାନେ ତାହାର ମାହାତ୍ମ୍ୟ ବା ସୁଖ୍ୟାତି। ସେହି ବଡ଼ ପରିଚୟକୁ ଏଠାରେ ଧୋବା ତୁଠ ପରି ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ସ୍ଥାନ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଦାବି କରାଯାଉଥିବା ଗୌରବ ଓ ସାଧାରଣ ବ୍ୟବହାରରେ ଦିଶୁଥିବା ଅବସ୍ଥାର ତୁଳନା ଆସେ। ଦୂରରୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସା ଶୁଣିବା ସହ ପାଖର ଛୋଟ କଥାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେଖିବାର ଅବକାଶ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି।
ready_drafts.english_summary: An ordinary shared place may reveal more than a grand claim of reputation.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ପ୍ରଶଂସା ସହ ସାଧାରଣ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ସ୍ଥାନ ମଧ୍ୟ ପରିଚୟ ଦେଇପାରେ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: A club advertises its excellent organisation, but leaves its shared workroom unusable. A member quotes the saying to suggest that the everyday space deserves attention before another publicity campaign.
ready_drafts.cultural_context: Historical occupational image is retained without making caste traits or purity claims. The headword supplies reputation; everyday-maintenance application is editorial. No measured sanitation, geography or community assessment is claimed.

ready_drafts.title: Kicking someone who has fallen
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: Who kicks after someone has fallen—may those hands and feet burn.
ready_drafts.explanation: The anger is directed at the person who adds a kick after a fall. The curse gives the protest force: a moment of vulnerability has been used for further harm. We read the line as condemning that cruelty, while preserving its harsh words as the historical quotation rather than a wish to injure someone now. In conversation it can rebuke piling ridicule or blame onto a person already in difficulty. That nonviolent application is editorial; the source’s literal image remains a kick.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ପଡ଼ିଯାଇଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରିବା ବଦଳରେ ଯିଏ ପୁଣି ଗୋଇଠା ମାରେ, ତାହା ପ୍ରତି ଏହି ରାଗ। ଶେଷର ଅଭିଶାପରେ ପ୍ରତିବାଦର ତୀବ୍ରତା ଦିଶେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ କଥାଟି ଅସହାୟ ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତରେ ଆଉ ଆଘାତ ଯୋଡ଼ିବାକୁ ନିନ୍ଦା କରେ। ଆଜି କାହାର ଅସୁବିଧା ଦେଖି ଅଧିକ ଉପହାସ କରିବା ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗରେ ଏହାକୁ କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ; ଶରୀରର କ୍ଷତି କରିବାକୁ ଆମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ ଭାବେ ନୁହେଁ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: The fierce protest condemns adding harm when someone is already vulnerable.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ବିପଦରେ ପଡ଼ିଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଆଉ ଆଘାତ ଦେବା ବିରୋଧରେ ତୀବ୍ର ପ୍ରତିବାଦ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: A team member makes a costly mistake and admits it. When others keep mocking him after the problem is resolved, a colleague quotes the saying to stop the piling-on, not to threaten anyone.
ready_drafts.cultural_context: The source labels the headword Sambalpur; this does not establish exclusive origin. Curse retained as quoted rhetoric, not endorsed retaliatory violence. No historical incident or speaker identified.

ready_drafts.title: Even the torn umbrella
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: A torn umbrella: taken to market, it could have brought money.
ready_drafts.explanation: The dictionary spells out the small possibility: the torn umbrella could be sold for money if taken to market. Damage has not automatically made it valueless. The conditional ending makes the value depend on taking it to market; it could sound practical or rueful, depending on the occasion. Our present-day reading asks whether something dismissed as useless still has an honest use or exchange value. It is not a guarantee that every broken object will sell, and the defect should not be hidden from a buyer.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ଛତାଟି ଚିରା, ତଥାପି ହାଟକୁ ନେଇ ବିକିଲେ ପଇସା ମିଳନ୍ତା ବୋଲି ଅଭିଧାନ ବୁଝାଇଛି। ଖରାପ ହୋଇଗଲା ମାତ୍ରେ ଜିନିଷଟିର ସବୁ ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଶେଷ ହୋଇନାହିଁ। “ହେତା”ରେ ହାଟକୁ ନେଇ ବିକିବାର ସର୍ତ୍ତ ସହ ପଇସା ମିଳିବାର ସମ୍ଭାବନା ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଫିଙ୍ଗିଦେବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଜିନିଷର ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ କାମକୁ ଭାବିବାର ଅବକାଶ ଅଛି।
ready_drafts.english_summary: The damaged object may still bring money if taken to market.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ଚିରା ଜିନିଷ ହାଟକୁ ନେଇ ବିକିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ପଇସା ମିଳିପାରେ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: During a clear-out, someone is about to discard an old umbrella whose frame can still be used. A friend quotes the line and suggests offering it openly as a damaged item to someone who repairs umbrellas.

ready_drafts.title: A fine shawl and forgotten faces
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: Is this the former Kahnei? With a fine soft shawl on the shoulder, does he recognise people?
ready_drafts.explanation: The question contrasts a remembered person with the way he now behaves. The fine shawl becomes the visible sign beside a failure to recognise others. Our reading hears a teasing accusation that improved appearance or standing has brought social distance. The line does not tell us that the cloth itself changes character, or that everyone whose circumstances improve becomes proud. Its force is directed at the particular person being addressed through this pointed question.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ଏ କି ସେଇ ପୂର୍ବର କହ୍ନେଇ—ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପୁରୁଣା ପରିଚୟ ଓ ଏବର ଆଚରଣ ମୁହାଁମୁହିଁ ହେଉଛି। କାନ୍ଧର ସରୁ କୋମଳ ଚାଦର ପାଖରେ ମଣିଷ ନ ଚିହ୍ନିବାର କଥା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ବେଶ ବା ସ୍ଥିତି ବଦଳିଲା ପରେ ପୁରୁଣା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଅବହେଳା କରିବା ଉପରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ପୋଷାକଟି ନିଜେ ଦୋଷୀ ନୁହେଁ; ତାହା ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା ଲୋକର ବ୍ୟବହାର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପଡ଼ୁଛି।
ready_drafts.english_summary: A changed appearance becomes an image for forgetting familiar people.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ବେଶ ବଦଳିଲା ପରେ ପରିଚିତ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଭୁଲିବାରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: After a promotion, a friend stops greeting the people who used to share lunch with him. One of them quotes the saying in a private conversation, teasing the new distance rather than the friend’s clothes.

ready_drafts.title: When lasting illness becomes invisible
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: They do not look towards the chronically ill person.
ready_drafts.explanation: The dictionary defines the person in the line as chronically ill. The statement records a harsh lack of attention, but its brief quotation gives no speaker or occasion to tell us whether the neglect was being observed, lamented or defended. Our reading uses it critically: a difficulty that lasts can cease to attract the attention given to a new crisis. That is a way to question neglect, not a reason to accept it or a claim that every family behaves this way.

ready_drafts.english_summary: Our critical reading questions attention fading while someone’s illness continues.

ready_drafts.title: A relationship questioned after loss
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: When the daughter dies, whose relative is the son-in-law?
ready_drafts.explanation: The question presents a relationship as if it depends entirely on the woman through whom it was formed. Her death becomes the point at which the son-in-law’s place is questioned. The dictionary explains kinship vocabulary, but supplies no family story or evidence that the question describes a universal custom. Our reading approaches it critically: loss can expose how narrowly people define belonging. It need not settle the answer for a real bereaved family, whose affection and obligations cannot be reduced to this rhetorical line.

ready_drafts.english_summary: Our critical reading questions a narrow account of belonging after a family loss.

ready_drafts.title: The bird, but not the trap
ready_drafts.literal_meaning: Has seen the dove, but has not seen the trap.
ready_drafts.explanation: The two halves separate familiarity with an attractive or ordinary sight from knowledge of the danger connected with it. Seeing the bird does not mean seeing the trap. In our reading, the line can warn against mistaking partial experience for a full understanding of a situation. It may also sound like a taunt to someone who thinks they already know enough. The dictionary identifies the bird but gives no trapping story; the modern application and tone are editorial possibilities, not proof of an original event.
ready_drafts.meaning_odia: ପକ୍ଷୀଟିକୁ ଦେଖିଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଫାନ୍ଦକୁ ଦେଖିନାହିଁ—ଦୁଇ ପ୍ରକାର ଜାଣିବାର ତଫାତ ଏଠାରେ ଆସେ। ଚିହ୍ନା ଜିନିଷଟିକୁ ଜାଣିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ା ବିପଦ ଅଜଣା ରହିପାରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଅଳ୍ପ ଅନୁଭବକୁ ପୂରା ଜ୍ଞାନ ଭାବିବା ବେଳେ କଥାଟି ସତର୍କ କରେ। କହିବାର ସ୍ୱର ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହା ଚେତାବନୀ ବା ଟିକିଏ ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟ ମଧ୍ୟ ହୋଇପାରେ।
ready_drafts.english_summary: Familiarity with what is visible may leave its accompanying danger unseen.
ready_drafts.odia_summary: ଦିଶୁଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ଚିହ୍ନିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହା ସହ ଥିବା ବିପଦ ଅଜଣା ରହିପାରେ।
ready_drafts.usage_example: Original imagined example: A new organiser knows how to book a hall and assumes the whole event will be easy. An experienced colleague quotes the line, then explains the overlooked cancellation conditions. The analogy concerns incomplete preparation, not an actual bird trap.
ready_drafts.cultural_context: The dictionary labels the headword Medinipur; this does not establish birthplace or exclusive use. Bird identified generically as dove from source, no taxonomic or trapping instruction. Figurative application is our close reading; no supplied traditional moral gloss.
